findings.title: Team admin/owner authorization uses AND instead of OR
findings.body: In addGuestsHandler, isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed as (await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...)). The variable name and access check intend to allow team admins OR team owners. Using && requires both checks to pass, so legitimate team admins or owners can be denied access. It also short-circuits the owner check when isTeamAdmin returns false.

findings.title: Server does not de-duplicate guest emails
findings.body: uniqueGuests filters only emails already attached to the booking or blacklisted; it does not remove duplicates from the incoming guests array, and the Zod schema does not enforce uniqueness. A direct API call with duplicate emails can create multiple attendee rows for the same booking, and concurrent requests can also create duplicates.

findings.title: Email addresses are not normalized before duplicate/blacklist checks
findings.body: Guest emails are compared to existing attendees and lowercased blacklist entries without being lowercased or trimmed first. Because email addresses are case-insensitive at least for the domain, Guest@Example.com can bypass a blacklist entry guest@example.com and can also be added as a duplicate of guest@example.com. Normalize emails before validation, persistence, and email sending.

findings.title: No booking-status check before adding guests
findings.body: The handler only verifies that the booking exists and that the caller has access. It does not reject cancelled, rejected, or otherwise inactive bookings. A direct API call can add attendees, attempt calendar updates, and send invitation emails for a cancelled or rejected event. The endpoint should restrict this mutation to appropriate active booking statuses.

findings.title: Organizer lookup fails for bookings without a userId
findings.body: The organizer is loaded with prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } }). If a booking has no userId, which the fallback suggests is possible, this queries user ID 0 and throws, producing a server error instead of handling the booking gracefully. The handler should either validate that a host exists or derive the organizer/team safely.

findings.title: No capacity check for seat-limited events
findings.body: The mutation adds attendees without checking booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot or the current attendee count. For event types with limited seats, a direct API call can overbook the booking by adding more attendees than the configured capacity.

findings.title: No rollback if calendar update fails after attendees are added
findings.body: Attendees are persisted before eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees is called. If the calendar update fails, the API returns an error but the added attendees remain in the database, leaving the booking record and external calendar inconsistent. Consider transactional handling, compensation, or at least validating/preparing external updates before persisting.

findings.title: Emails are sent using the original input instead of filtered uniqueGuests
findings.body: sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) passes the raw request emails rather than the normalized, de-duplicated uniqueGuests that were actually inserted. sendAddGuestsEmails uses that list to decide which attendees receive a full scheduled email versus a 'guests added' notification, so existing or blacklisted emails included in the request can cause the wrong email template to be sent.

findings.title: Calendar update uses requester's credentials instead of booking owner's
findings.body: EventManager is constructed with ctx.user and credentials from getUsersCredentials(ctx.user). When the caller is a team admin or an attendee rather than the booking owner, calendar updates may not have access to the organizer's calendar or may update the wrong calendar. The booking owner's credentials/references should be used when updating the booking's calendar event.

findings.title: No limit on number or length of guest emails
findings.body: guests: z.array(z.string().email()) has no max count and no per-email length limit. An authenticated client can submit a very large array, causing bulk attendee creation, many translation lookups, calendar updates, and mass email sending. Add a reasonable maximum array length and email string length.

findings.title: Add-guest emails ignore email-disable settings
findings.body: sendAddGuestsEmails does not accept or honor eventTypeMetadata disableStandardEmails settings, nor host/attendee email disabled flags, unlike other email-sending helpers. Event types configured to disable standard host or attendee emails will still send organizer and attendee emails when guests are added.

findings.title: Error toast fallback is unreachable and can show 'undefined'
findings.body: In onError, message is built as `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`. If err.data?.code is undefined, the toast displays 'undefined: ...'. Also, because the template string is always truthy, `message || t('unable_to_add_guests')` never falls back to the intended generic error message.

Closing via Dialog onOpenChange, such as Escape or clicking outside, leaves previous email values and validation error state behind. isInvalidEmail is also not cleared when the user edits the email fields, so a stale error can remain visible after correction.
